instruction: Change the font of all italicized words in the document to Arial, while keeping the rest of the text in Times New Roman.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully used Find & Replace with formatting to change all italic text from 12pt to 14pt in LibreOffice Writer document. Used the Replace with Formatting dialog to target italic style and set replacement size to 14.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use Find & Replace with formatting options in LibreOffice Writer, can selectively modify font properties of styled text, can navigate formatting dialogs
metadata.task_rationale: Tests same Find & Replace workflow but targets font name instead of font size. Agent proved it can use formatting-based search, so changing a different font property is a natural related variation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all italic text font to Arial while keeping non-italic text in Times New Roman. Getter extracts font names of both italic and non-italic runs. Metric checks proportion of italic runs using Arial (0.5 weight) and proportion of non-italic runs using Times New Roman (0.5 weight) for partial credit. [Fixed: added non-italic font verification to cover both instruction requirements]

scoring_breakdown.italic_font_match: 0.5 - proportion of italic runs with Arial font
scoring_breakdown.non_italic_font_match: 0.5 - proportion of non-italic runs with Times New Roman font

fix_history: Fix 1: Corrected MD5 hash suffix from truncated 8-char 'dd1b6aeb' to full 32-char 'f2fb15859784992fd6cf15bd171d4b91' computed from 'e246f6d8-78d7-44ac-b668-fcf47946cb50|0'. Updated getter function name, metric function name, evaluator references, file paths, and new_functions_paths.
Fix 2: Removed old getter/metric functions with invalid 'dd1b6aeb' hash suffix that were still present in the directory, causing rule-based validation to fail.

Fix 3: Added non-italic font verification. Updated getter to collect both italic and non-italic run fonts. Updated metric to check both requirements with partial scoring (0.5 italic=Arial + 0.5 non-italic=Times New Roman). Added expected_non_italic_font to rules.

llm_judge_reasons: Coverage is now complete: Both instruction requirements are verified - (1) italic text font changed to Arial (0.5 weight) and (2) non-italic text remains Times New Roman (0.5 weight).
Getter logic correctly iterates all paragraphs/runs, skips empty whitespace runs, separates italic vs non-italic runs, and collects font names for both categories.

Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': directly accesses expected.get('expected_font') and expected.get('expected_non_italic_font'), which is correct since framework passes rules dict directly.
Proportional scoring with 0.5/0.5 split is reasonable and provides partial credit for each requirement.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.

Significant concern: run.font.name returns None for runs that inherit font from paragraph/document style. If the document's default style is Times New Roman (common), non-italic runs will have run.font.name=None. The metric counts None != 'Times New Roman' as non-matching, potentially scoring 0 on the non-italic check even when text correctly displays in Times New Roman. This could cap the total score at 0.5 for a correctly completed task.
The italic font check is less affected since the agent must explicitly set Arial on italic runs, which typically sets run.font.name at the run level.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: In the getter, resolve None font names by falling back to paragraph style font: if run.font.name is None, check para.style.font.name or the document's default style. This handles font inheritance correctly.
Alternatively, use python-docx's run.font.name with a fallback chain: run.font.name -> paragraph.style.font.name -> document.styles['Normal'].font.name to get the effective font for each run.
validation.fix_applied: Fix 3: Extended getter to collect both italic and non-italic font names. Extended metric with partial scoring (0.5 italic=Arial + 0.5 non-italic=Times New Roman). Added expected_non_italic_font to rules.
